changes.historical_text: Decrease 1 selected monster's DEF by 500 points during the turn this card is activated.
changes.summary: Era damage-step legality, no text difference: the goat script carries EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL where the modern script carries EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP, moving the card's Damage Step activation window from the sub-steps before damage calculation (modern, PHASE_DAMAGE) to the damage-calculation sub-step itself (PHASE_DAMAGE_CAL). Nothing else differs behaviourally: the goat s.condition (`Duel.GetCurrentPhase()~=PHASE_DAMAGE or not Duel.IsDamageCalculated()`) is the De Morgan equivalent of aux.StatChangeDamageStepCondition (utility.lua line 1413: `not (Duel.IsPhase(PHASE_DAMAGE) and Duel.IsDamageCalculated())`), and `RESET_EVENT+RESETS_STANDARD+RESET_PHASE+PHASE_END` is the literal expansion of RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END (constant.lua line 300). Chronology of this ruling is unresolved.

review.notes: The chain starts at lineage v0 (MRL-050, 2002-09-16), carried exactly by both the goat cdb entry and the pinned modern cards.cdb, so no text transition is recorded. The lineage oscillates cosmetically: v1 (SRL-EN050, Master Collection Volume 1, 2004-12-01) reads 'Decrease 1 face-up monster's DEF by 500 points until the end of this turn' and v2 (SRL-050, Legendary Collection, 2010) returns to the v0 wording; same resolution throughout. Relationship to the engine layer, since EdisonFormat lists the 7-timing damage step among the era's global rules differences: the activation window here is per-card script data (the effect's EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP / EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL property), which an ocgcore rule profile cannot rewrite, so this is ruling and not engine - it needs the variant script. Corroboration that the flag choice is deliberate rather than an oversight: 25 goat variants set EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL, 23 of them without EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP, while 0 official scripts in the repo set DAMAGE_CAL without also setting DAMAGE_STEP.
